import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.14

by O. H. Kegel

b) Assume a group $G$ is existentially closed in one of the classes
$L\mathfrak{N}^{+}$, $L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$, $L\mathfrak{S}^{+}$, $L\mathfrak{S}$ of,
respectively, all locally nilpotent torsion-free groups, all locally soluble $\pi$-groups,
all locally soluble torsion-free groups, or all locally soluble groups.
Is it true that $G$ is characteristically simple?

The notebook remarks that the existential closedness of $G$ is a local property, so it seems
difficult to obtain global properties of $G$ from it. Part a) of the problem is solved and has
been moved to the Archive of the notebook; it is not stated here.

A group $G$ is *existentially closed* in a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups if $G \in \mathfrak{X}$
and every finite system of equations and inequations with coefficients in $G$ that has a solution
in some group $H \in \mathfrak{X}$ containing $G$ as a subgroup already has a solution in $G$.
A group is *characteristically simple* if its only characteristic subgroups are the trivial
subgroup and the whole group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.14»

/-- A finite system of equations and inequations over the group `G` in `n` unknowns. Words are
elements of the free group on the alphabet `G ⊕ Fin n`: letters from `G` are the coefficients and
letters from `Fin n` are the unknowns. A word `w ∈ eqs` stands for the equation `w = 1` and a word
`w ∈ neqs` stands for the inequation `w ≠ 1`. -/
structure EqSystem (G : Type u) [Group G] (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The words `w` standing for the equations `w = 1`. -/
  eqs : Finset (FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n))
  /-- The words `w` standing for the inequations `w ≠ 1`. -/
  neqs : Finset (FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n))

/-- The assignment `v` of the unknowns is a solution in the group `H` of the system `S` over `G`,
where the coefficients from `G` are interpreted in `H` via the homomorphism `f`: every word of
`S.eqs` evaluates to `1` and no word of `S.neqs` evaluates to `1`. -/
def EqSystem.IsSolution {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] {n : ℕ} (S : EqSystem G n)
    (f : G →* H) (v : Fin n → H) : Prop :=
  (∀ w ∈ S.eqs, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim f v) w = 1) ∧
    (∀ w ∈ S.neqs, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim f v) w ≠ 1)

/-- A group `G` is *existentially closed* in the class `𝒳` of groups if `G` belongs to `𝒳`
and, for every group `H` in `𝒳` containing `G` as a subgroup (i.e. with an injective
homomorphism `G →* H`), every finite system of equations and inequations with coefficients in
`G` that has a solution in `H` already has a solution in `G`. -/
def IsExistentiallyClosedIn (𝒳 : ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], Prop) (G : Type u) [Group G] :
    Prop :=
  𝒳 G ∧ ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], 𝒳 H → ∀ f : G →* H, Function.Injective f →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : EqSystem G n), (∃ v : Fin n → H, S.IsSolution f v) →
      ∃ v : Fin n → G, S.IsSolution (MonoidHom.id G) v

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A group is *locally soluble* (locally solvable) if every finitely generated subgroup is
soluble. -/
def IsLocallySolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsSolvable H

/-- A group is *torsion-free* if its only element of finite order is the identity.

This is weaker than Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree` (injectivity of `x ↦ x ^ n` for `n ≠ 0`), which
for non-abelian groups additionally demands uniqueness of roots. -/
def IsTorsionFreeGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1

/-- For a set of primes `π`, a group `G` is a *`π`-group* if every element of `G` has finite order
and every prime divisor of the order of every element of `G` lies in `π`. -/
def IsPiGroup (π : Set Nat.Primes) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g ∧ ∀ p : Nat.Primes, (p : ℕ) ∣ orderOf g → p ∈ π

/-- A group is *characteristically simple* if its only characteristic subgroups are the trivial
subgroup `⊥` and the whole group `⊤`. -/
def IsCharacteristicallySimple (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.Characteristic → H = ⊥ ∨ H = ⊤

/-- A group existentially closed in a class of groups belongs to that class. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsExistentiallyClosedIn.mem {𝒳 : ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], Prop} {G : Type u} [Group G]
    (h : IsExistentiallyClosedIn 𝒳 G) : 𝒳 G :=
  h.1

/-- A simple group is characteristically simple. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsCharacteristicallySimple.of_isSimpleGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsSimpleGroup G] :
    IsCharacteristicallySimple G :=
  fun H _ => IsSimpleGroup.eq_bot_or_eq_top_of_normal H (Subgroup.normal_of_characteristic H)

/--
Assume a group $G$ is existentially closed in one of the classes $L\mathfrak{N}^{+}$,
$L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$, $L\mathfrak{S}^{+}$, $L\mathfrak{S}$ of, respectively, all locally
nilpotent torsion-free groups, all locally soluble $\pi$-groups (for some set of primes $\pi$),
all locally soluble torsion-free groups, or all locally soluble groups. Is it true that $G$ is
characteristically simple?

The set of primes $\pi$ is required to be nonempty: for $\pi = \emptyset$ the class
$L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$ consists of the trivial groups only, and the question would degenerate to
the convention on whether the trivial group is characteristically simple.
-/

modeling_decisions: Existential closedness is formalized via finite systems of equations and inequations with coefficients in G (words in FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n)), which is equivalent to the model-theoretic formulation with existential formulas with parameters from G (DNF + distributing ∃ over ∨). Inequations are included, as in the standard notion of 'existentially closed' (as opposed to 'algebraically closed').

'G ≤ H' is modeled as an injective group homomorphism G →* H with H in the same universe as G (Type). This is harmless for all four classes: each is closed under subgroups, and a solution in a large H lives in the subgroup generated by the image of G and finitely many elements, which has small cardinality.
IsExistentiallyClosedIn includes the requirement G ∈ 𝒳, following the standard definition.
Torsion-free is defined as 'only the identity has finite order' (IsTorsionFreeGroup), deliberately NOT Mathlib's IsMulTorsionFree, which for non-abelian groups is the stronger unique-roots property.

The set of primes π is taken as π : Set Nat.Primes and required to be nonempty. For π = ∅ the class L𝔖_π consists only of trivial groups, the trivial group is then existentially closed in it, and the answer would depend purely on the convention of whether the trivial group is characteristically simple; excluding this degenerate case is robust to either convention. For nonempty π (and for the other three classes) existentially closed groups are automatically nontrivial, so the chosen definition of IsCharacteristicallySimple (no Nontrivial requirement) agrees with the alternative convention on all groups the statement actually quantifies over.

The primary slot is stated with a disjunctive hypothesis ('existentially closed in one of the classes'), with π existentially quantified inside the disjunct; this is equivalent to the conjunction over the four classes with π universally quantified.
Locally nilpotent / locally soluble mean every finitely generated subgroup (Subgroup.FG) is nilpotent / soluble.

by O. H. Kegel

Terminology. A group $G$ is *existentially closed* in a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups if
$G \in \mathfrak{X}$ and every finite system of equations and inequations with coefficients in
$G$ (in finitely many unknowns) that has a solution in some group $H \in \mathfrak{X}$ containing
$G$ already has a solution in $G$. A group is *locally nilpotent* (resp. *locally soluble*) if
all its finitely generated subgroups are nilpotent (resp. soluble). It is *torsion-free* if $1$
is its only element of finite order. For a set of primes $\pi$, it is a *$\pi$-group* if every
element has finite order all of whose prime divisors lie in $\pi$. A group is
*characteristically simple* if its only characteristic subgroups are the trivial subgroup and the
whole group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.14»

universe u

variable {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H]

/-- A class of groups, i.e. a property of groups. -/
abbrev GroupClass := (H : Type u) → [Group H] → Prop

/-- A finite system of equations and inequations over the group `G` in the `n` unknowns
`x_0, …, x_{n-1}`. Each side of an equation or inequation is a word in the unknowns and in the
elements of `G`, i.e. an element of the free group on `G ⊕ Fin n`. A pair `(u, v)` in `eqs`
stands for the equation `u = v` and a pair `(u, v)` in `neqs` stands for the inequation `u ≠ v`. -/
structure FiniteSystem (G : Type*) (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The equations of the system. -/
  eqs : Finset (FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n) × FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n))
  /-- The inequations of the system. -/
  neqs : Finset (FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n) × FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n))

namespace FiniteSystem

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- Evaluation of words over `G` in a group `H` at the tuple `x : Fin n → H`, where the
coefficients from `G` are interpreted in `H` via the homomorphism `φ : G →* H`. -/
def eval (φ : G →* H) (x : Fin n → H) : FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n) →* H :=
  FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim φ x)

/-- The tuple `x : Fin n → H` is a solution of the system `S` in the group `H`, where the
coefficients from `G` are interpreted in `H` via `φ`. -/
def IsSolution (S : FiniteSystem G n) (φ : G →* H) (x : Fin n → H) : Prop :=
  (∀ p ∈ S.eqs, eval φ x p.1 = eval φ x p.2) ∧ ∀ p ∈ S.neqs, eval φ x p.1 ≠ eval φ x p.2

/-- The system `S` has a solution in the group `H`, where the coefficients from `G` are
interpreted in `H` via `φ`. -/
def HasSolution (S : FiniteSystem G n) (φ : G →* H) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : Fin n → H, S.IsSolution φ x

end FiniteSystem

/-- A group `G` is *existentially closed* in a class of groups `𝔛` if `G ∈ 𝔛` and every finite
system of equations and inequations with coefficients in `G` that has a solution in some group
`H ∈ 𝔛` containing `G` (i.e. into which `G` embeds) already has a solution in `G`. -/
def IsExistentiallyClosedIn (𝔛 : GroupClass.{u}) (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  𝔛 G ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : FiniteSystem G n) (H : Type u) [Group H] (φ : G →* H),
    Function.Injective φ → 𝔛 H → S.HasSolution φ → S.HasSolution (MonoidHom.id G)

/-- A group is *torsion-free* if `1` is its only element of finite order. (For non-abelian groups
this is weaker than Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree`, which asks for unique roots.) -/
def IsTorsionFree (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if all its finitely generated subgroups are nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ K : Subgroup G, K.FG → Group.IsNilpotent K

/-- A group is *locally soluble* if all its finitely generated subgroups are soluble. -/
def IsLocallySolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ K : Subgroup G, K.FG → IsSolvable K

/-- For a set of primes `π`, a group is a *`π`-group* if each of its elements has finite order
all of whose prime divisors lie in `π`. -/
def IsPiGroup (π : Set Nat.Primes) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g ∧ ∀ p : Nat.Primes, (p : ℕ) ∣ orderOf g → p ∈ π

/-- A group is *characteristically simple* if its only characteristic subgroups are the trivial
subgroup and the whole group. With this definition the trivial group is characteristically
simple. -/
def IsCharacteristicallySimple (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ K : Subgroup G, K.Characteristic → K = ⊥ ∨ K = ⊤

theorem IsTorsionFree.of_isMulTorsionFree [IsMulTorsionFree G] : IsTorsionFree G :=
  fun _ hg => by_contra fun h => not_isOfFinOrder_of_isMulTorsionFree h hg

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent [Group.IsNilpotent G] : IsLocallyNilpotent G :=

# Conjecture 8.14

$L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$, $L\mathfrak{S}^{+}$, $L\mathfrak{S}$ of, respectively, all locally
nilpotent torsion-free groups, all locally soluble $\pi$-groups, all locally soluble
torsion-free groups, or all locally soluble groups. Is it true that $G$ is characteristically
simple?

Here a group $G$ is *existentially closed* in a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups if
$G \in \mathfrak{X}$ and every finite system of equations and inequations with coefficients in
$G$ which has a solution in some $\mathfrak{X}$-group containing $G$ already has a solution in
$G$. A group is *characteristically simple* if its only characteristic subgroups are the trivial
subgroup and the whole group.

Part a) of Problem 8.14 is in the Archive of solved problems of the notebook and is not posed
here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.14»

universe u

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A group is *locally soluble* if every finitely generated subgroup is soluble. -/
def IsLocallySolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsSolvable H

/-- A group is *torsion-free* if its only element of finite order is the identity.

This is the usual group-theoretic notion. It is weaker than Mathlib's `IsMulTorsionFree`
(injectivity of $x \mapsto x^n$ for $n \neq 0$) for non-abelian groups: the torsion-free
metabelian Klein bottle group $\langle a, b \mid aba^{-1} = b^{-1} \rangle$ satisfies
$(ab)^2 = a^2$ with $ab \neq a$. -/
def IsTorsionFree (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1

/-- For a set `π` of primes, a group is a *`π`-group* if every element has finite order and
every prime divisor of the order of every element belongs to `π`.

Here `π` is an arbitrary set of natural numbers; its non-prime elements play no role, so a
`π`-group is the same thing as a `(π ∩ primes)`-group. -/
def IsPiGroup (π : Set ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ orderOf g → p ∈ π

/-- A group is *characteristically simple* if its only characteristic subgroups are the trivial
subgroup `⊥` and the whole group `⊤`.

With this convention the trivial group is characteristically simple. This convention only
matters for the class $L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$ with $\pi$ containing no prime, which consists of
the trivial groups alone; all other groups existentially closed in one of the classes of
Problem 8.14 are non-trivial. -/
def IsCharacteristicallySimple (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.Characteristic → H = ⊥ ∨ H = ⊤

/-- Evaluation of a word `w` in the free group on `Fin n ⊕ G` in a group `H`: the letters
`Sum.inl i` (the unknowns `x_i`) are replaced by `x i : H` and the letters `Sum.inr g` (the
coefficients from `G`) by `f g`, where `f : G →* H`.

The equation (resp. inequation) `w = 1` (resp. `w ≠ 1`) in the unknowns `x_0, …, x_{n-1}` with
coefficients in `G` is then the assertion `evalWord f x w = 1` (resp. `evalWord f x w ≠ 1`).
Every equation `u = v` between words is of this form since `u = v ↔ u * v⁻¹ = 1`. -/
def evalWord {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] {n : ℕ} (f : G →* H) (x : Fin n → H)
    (w : FreeGroup (Fin n ⊕ G)) : H :=
  FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x f) w

/-- A group `G` is *existentially closed* in a class `𝔛` of groups if `G` belongs to `𝔛` and
every finite system of equations `w = 1` (`w ∈ E`) and inequations `w ≠ 1` (`w ∈ I`) in
finitely many unknowns with coefficients in `G` which has a solution in some `𝔛`-group `H`
containing `G` (i.e. equipped with an injective homomorphism `G →* H`) already has a solution
in `G`.

harmless that `H` ranges over groups in the same universe as `G`: a solution in `H` lies in the
subgroup generated by `G` together with the solution. -/
def IsExistentiallyClosedIn (𝔛 : (H : Type u) → [Group H] → Prop) (G : Type u) [Group G] :
    Prop :=
  𝔛 G ∧
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (E I : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n ⊕ G))),
      (∃ (H : Type u) (_ : Group H) (f : G →* H) (x : Fin n → H),
        𝔛 H ∧ Function.Injective f ∧
          (∀ w ∈ E, evalWord f x w = 1) ∧ (∀ w ∈ I, evalWord f x w ≠ 1)) →
      ∃ x : Fin n → G,
        (∀ w ∈ E, evalWord (MonoidHom.id G) x w = 1) ∧
          (∀ w ∈ I, evalWord (MonoidHom.id G) x w ≠ 1)

torsion-free groups, locally soluble $\pi$-groups, locally soluble
torsion-free groups, or locally soluble groups, is it characteristically

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«8.14»

/-- A group is locally nilpotent if every subgroup generated by finitely many
elements is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → G), Group.IsNilpotent (Subgroup.closure (Set.range x))

/-- A group is locally soluble if every subgroup generated by finitely many
elements is soluble. -/
def IsLocallySoluble (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → G), IsSolvable (Subgroup.closure (Set.range x))

/-- A $\pi$-group is a torsion group in which every prime divisor of the order
of every element belongs to $\pi$. -/
def IsPiGroup (π : Set Nat.Primes) (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g ∧
    ∀ (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime), p ∣ orderOf g → (⟨p, hp⟩ : Nat.Primes) ∈ π

/-- A group is characteristically simple if its only characteristic subgroups
are the bottom and top subgroups. Under this convention, the trivial group is
characteristically simple. -/
def IsCharacteristicallySimple (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.Characteristic → H = ⊥ ∨ H = ⊤

/-- A group class is a predicate on groups. -/
abbrev GroupClass := (G : Type) → [Group G] → Prop

/-- A group $G$ is existentially closed in a class $C$ if $G$ belongs to $C$
and every finite system of equations and inequations over $G$ that has a
solution in a group in $C$ containing an isomorphic copy of $G$ already has a
solution in $G$.

A system with `n` variables is represented by finite families of words in the
free group on `Fin n ⊕ G`; the second summand supplies coefficients from $G$.
Each equation says that its word is one, and each inequation says that its word
is not one. -/
def IsExistentiallyClosedIn (C : GroupClass) (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  C G ∧
    ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], C H →
      ∀ (ι : G →* H), Function.Injective ι →
        ∀ (n equationCount inequationCount : ℕ)
          (equations : Fin equationCount → FreeGroup (Fin n ⊕ G))
          (inequations : Fin inequationCount → FreeGroup (Fin n ⊕ G)),
          (∃ x : Fin n → H,
              (∀ j, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x ι) (equations j) = 1) ∧
              (∀ j, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x ι) (inequations j) ≠ 1)) →

              (∀ j, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x (fun g ↦ g)) (equations j) = 1) ∧

  fun G _ ↦ IsLocallySoluble G ∧ IsMulTorsionFree G

  fun G _ ↦ IsLocallySoluble G

/-!
# Conjecture 8.14

by O. H. Kegel

b) Assume a group $G$ is existentially closed in one of the classes $L\mathfrak{N}^{+}$,
$L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$, $L\mathfrak{S}^{+}$, $L\mathfrak{S}$ of, respectively, all locally
nilpotent torsion-free groups, all locally soluble $\pi$-groups, all locally soluble
torsion-free groups, or all locally soluble groups. Is it true that $G$ is characteristically
simple?

The existential closedness of $G$ is a local property, thus it seems difficult to obtain
global properties of $G$ from it. See also Archive, 8.14 a.

Here a group $G$ in a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups is *existentially closed in $\mathfrak{X}$*
if every finite system of equations and inequations with coefficients in $G$ that has a solution
in some $\mathfrak{X}$-group containing $G$ already has a solution in $G$. A group is
*characteristically simple* if its only characteristic subgroups are the trivial subgroup and
the whole group. Part a) of the problem is solved and is only cross-referenced to the Archive
in the notebook, so only part b) is stated here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.14»

universe u

section Definitions

variable (G : Type*) [Group G]

/-- A group is *torsion-free* if its only element of finite order is the identity. -/
def IsTorsionFree : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A group is *locally soluble* if every finitely generated subgroup is soluble. -/
def IsLocallySolvable : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → IsSolvable H

/-- For a set of primes $\pi$, a group is a *$\pi$-group* if every element has finite order
and every prime divisor of the order of every element lies in $\pi$. -/
def IsPiGroup (π : Set Nat.Primes) : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g ∧ ∀ p : Nat.Primes, (p : ℕ) ∣ orderOf g → p ∈ π

/-- A group is *characteristically simple* if its only characteristic subgroups are the trivial
subgroup and the whole group. With this convention the trivial group is characteristically
simple. -/
def IsCharacteristicallySimple : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.Characteristic → H = ⊥ ∨ H = ⊤

/-- The class $L\mathfrak{N}^{+}$ of all locally nilpotent torsion-free groups. -/
def LNPlus : Prop :=
  IsLocallyNilpotent G ∧ IsTorsionFree G

/-- The class $L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$ of all locally soluble $\pi$-groups. -/
def LSPi (π : Set Nat.Primes) : Prop :=
  IsLocallySolvable G ∧ IsPiGroup G π

/-- The class $L\mathfrak{S}^{+}$ of all locally soluble torsion-free groups. -/
def LSPlus : Prop :=
  IsLocallySolvable G ∧ IsTorsionFree G

/-- The class $L\mathfrak{S}$ of all locally soluble groups. -/
def LS : Prop :=
  IsLocallySolvable G

variable {G}

/-- A finite system of equations $w = 1$ (for $w \in E$) and inequations $w \neq 1$ (for
$w \in I$) in $n$ unknowns with coefficients in $G$ has a solution in the group $K$, where the
coefficients are transported along `f : G →* K`.

A word $w$ is an element of the free group on `G ⊕ Fin n`: `Sum.inl g` is the constant $g \in G$
and `Sum.inr i` is the $i$-th unknown. -/
def HasSolution {n : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Group K] (f : G →* K)
    (E I : Finset (FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : Fin n → K,
    (∀ w ∈ E, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim f x) w = 1) ∧
      ∀ w ∈ I, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim f x) w ≠ 1

/-- A group $G$ is *existentially closed in the class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups* if $G$ belongs to
$\mathfrak{X}$ and every finite system of equations and inequations with coefficients in $G$ that
has a solution in some $\mathfrak{X}$-group $H$ containing $G$ (that is, $G$ embeds in $H$)
already has a solution in $G$. -/
def IsExistentiallyClosedIn (𝔛 : ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], Prop) (G : Type u) [Group G] :
    Prop :=
  𝔛 G ∧ ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], 𝔛 H → ∀ f : G →* H, Function.Injective f →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (E I : Finset (FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n))),
      HasSolution f E I → HasSolution (MonoidHom.id G) E I

end Definitions

modeling_decisions: Existential closure is formalized via finite systems of equations w = 1 and inequations w ≠ 1 in finitely many unknowns with coefficients in G (words in FreeGroup (G ⊕ Fin n)). Equations u = v are covered by u v⁻¹ = 1, and existential formulas with parameters reduce to such systems via disjunctive normal form, so this matches the model-theoretic definition; it is the definition in the decomposition notes and the standard one (Higman–Scott, Kegel).

'X-group containing G' is modeled as a group H in the same universe as G together with an injective MonoidHom G →* H. Restricting H to the same universe is harmless for the four classes at hand since they are subgroup-closed and isomorphism-invariant and a finite solution set generates a small subgroup, but the definition IsExistentiallyClosedIn is universe-restricted in general.
G is required to belong to the class 𝔛 as part of 'existentially closed in 𝔛' (standard convention, also in the decomposition notes).

Torsion-free is 'no nontrivial element of finite order' (∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1), deliberately NOT Mathlib's IsMulTorsionFree (unique roots), which is strictly stronger for non-nilpotent groups and would change the classes L𝔖⁺ (and formally L𝔑⁺).

Characteristically simple is 'only characteristic subgroups are ⊥ and ⊤' with no Nontrivial requirement. A trivial group is existentially closed in one of the four classes only when the class consists of trivial groups, i.e. only for L𝔖_π with π = ∅; under this convention that degenerate instance is vacuously true and does not distort the answer, whereas the Nontrivial convention would make the conjunction trivially false for degenerate reasons. π is quantified over all Set Nat.Primes without a nonemptiness restriction, as in the source.
π-group: every element has finite order and all prime divisors of orderOf g lie in π (π : Set Nat.Primes). The IsOfFinOrder conjunct is essential since orderOf g = 0 for elements of infinite order.
Locally nilpotent / locally soluble use Subgroup.FG together with Mathlib's Group.IsNilpotent / IsSolvable on the subgroup coerced to a type.

The main slot is stated with a disjunctive hypothesis (∃ π inside the second disjunct) rather than as a conjunction of four statements; these are logically equivalent and the disjunction mirrors the text 'in one of the classes'.
Groups are quantified over Type (not Type*), following the existing Kourovka files in the repository.

new_definitions.why_needed: G is existentially closed in a class 𝔛 : ∀ (H : Type u) [Group H], Prop if 𝔛 G holds and for every 𝔛-group H with an injective hom f : G →* H, every finite system solvable in H (via f) is solvable in G. Not in Mathlib or the repo.

kourovka.«8.14».parts.b.why: Stated as answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G, (EC in L𝔑⁺ ∨ (∃ π, EC in L𝔖_π) ∨ EC in L𝔖⁺ ∨ EC in L𝔖) → characteristically simple, mirroring the disjunctive hypothesis 'existentially closed in one of the classes' with π implicitly universally quantified. All notions (existential closure in a class, locally nilpotent/soluble, torsion-free, π-group, characteristically simple) are bespoke since Mathlib has none.

kourovka.«8.14».parts.b.variants.locally.why: ∀ G, IsExistentiallyClosedIn LNPlus G → IsCharacteristicallySimple G, where LNPlus G := IsLocallyNilpotent G ∧ IsTorsionFree G.
∀ G, IsExistentiallyClosedIn LS G → IsCharacteristicallySimple G, where LS G := IsLocallySolvable G.

∀ (π : Set Nat.Primes) G, IsExistentiallyClosedIn (LSPi · π) G → IsCharacteristicallySimple G. π is an arbitrary set of primes (no nonemptiness restriction, as in the source); the π = ∅ degenerate case is handled by the documented convention that the trivial group is characteristically simple, so it does not distort the answer.
∀ G, IsExistentiallyClosedIn LSPlus G → IsCharacteristicallySimple G, where LSPlus G := IsLocallySolvable G ∧ IsTorsionFree G.

statement_blocks.kourovka.«8.14».parts.b:
/--
Assume a group $G$ is existentially closed in one of the classes $L\mathfrak{N}^{+}$,
$L\mathfrak{S}_{\pi}$, $L\mathfrak{S}^{+}$, $L\mathfrak{S}$ of, respectively, all locally
nilpotent torsion-free groups, all locally soluble $\pi$-groups, all locally soluble
torsion-free groups, or all locally soluble groups. Is it true that $G$ is characteristically
simple?

Here $\pi$ ranges over all sets of primes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.14».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
      (IsExistentiallyClosedIn LNPlus G ∨
        (∃ π : Set Nat.Primes, IsExistentiallyClosedIn (LSPi · π) G) ∨
        IsExistentiallyClosedIn LSPlus G ∨
        IsExistentiallyClosedIn LS G) →
      IsCharacteristicallySimple G := by
  sorry
